description: Canonical queue of hard-but-high-value engineering items for future CIEP passes. Seeded 2026-07-07 from an external planning doc (task-1..task-15, not shipped in this archive) covering the Pass 1-35 monorepo and Pass 1-4 standalone-harness audit tracks, then extended in Pass 38 (task-16..task-30) with additional adversarial/consistency/concurrency tasks derived directly from this codebase's own service inventory (chaos-monkey, circuit-breaker, semantic-dag, trust-ledger, skill-exchange, retry, prompt-registry, and others). One task per pass, per the CIEP protocol: pick the highest-priority task with status 'queued' and no unresolved 'blockedBy', run an Impact Analysis, implement, validate, update 06-CHANGELOG.md with a new numbered pass, then set this task's status to 'done' in the same pass. Do not start a second task in the same pass. Use scripts/task-queue.mjs to read/update this file rather than hand-editing where possible. Rounds 3-5 of the external free-tier infrastructure survey (LLM/multimodal race candidates, CI caching, secrets management, security/code-intelligence/QA APIs, feature flags, license-data cross-checks, and misc operational utility APIs) were folded into the queue in this pass as task-31 through task-45, split between owner-decision tasks (mirroring task-3's framing) and keyless/low-friction network-gated implementation tasks. Extended again outside the normal pass cycle (2026-07-08) with task-47..task-54, seeded from two external planning notes (a free-compute energy-taxonomy survey and a zero-cost infrastructure survey) plus two direct owner requests: an admin-facing panel to resolve owner-decision-gated tasks without hand-editing this file, and a readyToArchive/archive mechanism so verified-done tasks can be pruned from the active view without ever deleting history. See tasks/AGENT-PRINCIPLES.md for a new standing instruction, added the same day: before implementing any task exactly as worded, the assigned agent must first spend a short analysis step considering whether a better, simpler, cheaper, or safer approach exists, and record that reasoning in the pass's changelog entry.

tasks.title: Port ECOS sacred-file MD5-integrity pattern to Qodo's critical files
tasks.summary: Add hash-manifest integrity verification for the repo's highest blast-radius files (phase state machine, path-guard, audit/kill-switch primitives, AI-contract schemas).
tasks.whyHard: Moderate effort; proven pattern from a sibling project (ECOS) needed adaptation, not invention.
tasks.notes: Implemented in packages/agent/src/services/sacred-file-integrity.ts, upgraded MD5 -> SHA-256 to match this repo's existing audit-log.ts primitive. See 06-CHANGELOG.md Pass 36 for full impact analysis.

tasks.title: Tier 2/3 infrastructure keep-or-cut decision
tasks.summary: An explicit yes/no on Redis, R2, Vercel canary, Cloudflare Worker, QStash, using the cost-tier table in 03-ARCHITECTURE.md as the starting point.
tasks.whyHard: Organizational, not technical -- needs an actual owner decision, not more code.
tasks.notes: Most tractable next step for a network-less sandbox pass, but the deliverable is a documented decision (in 03-ARCHITECTURE.md), not new code -- do not invent code changes to make this look more like an engineering pass than it is.

tasks.title: Reconcile the two changelog numbering tracks
tasks.summary: 06-CHANGELOG.md has monorepo passes numbered with '## Pass N' headers (currently up to 36) and a separate standalone-harness/documentation track numbered 1-4 with '# Pass N' headers. Decide: merge the numbering, or explicitly rename one track.
tasks.whyHard: Not technically hard -- just needs a deliberate decision before more passes accumulate under the ambiguous scheme.
tasks.notes: Tractable in any sandbox. Touches only 06-CHANGELOG.md headers and CONSOLIDATION-NOTES.md; no source code impact.

tasks.title: Red-team the obfuscator / privacy-mode boundary
tasks.summary: Adversarially attempt to leak real symbol names past QODO_PRIVACY_MODE=strict by attacking the hasUnmappedTokens / reconstitutePatch ordering invariant (Do Not Touch List item 3 in 03-ARCHITECTURE.md).
tasks.whyHard: "We wrote it correctly" and "we tried to break it and couldn't" are very different confidence levels; this is the highest-consequence subsystem in the repo and a leak here is silent and retroactive.
tasks.notes: Implemented in Pass 45. Added packages/agent/tests/obfuscator-redteam.test.ts with adversarial tests for prefix-token substitution, function/class/import/property-access/comment/string leak paths, and the hasUnmappedTokens ordering invariant. Fixed reconstituteCode prefix-substitution bug (sort tokens by length descending). Hardened coder.ts to skip cross-repo reference patches when a privacy mapping is active. See 06-CHANGELOG.md Pass 45.

tasks.title: Adversarial test the audit-log hash chain itself
tasks.summary: Attempt to forge an entry or replay a truncated audit-log.ts NDJSON log and confirm verifyAuditChain actually catches it.
tasks.whyHard: Requires writing an adversarial suite against your own tamper-detection code, not a happy-path one.
tasks.notes: Implemented in packages/agent/tests/adversarial-audit-log.test.ts. 16 adversarial test cases covering payload/actor/timestamp/seq/prevHash/event mutation, full re-hash forge, cascading re-hash, middle deletion, entry injection, replay, tail/head truncation (documented design limits), corrupt JSON, zeroed hash, full fabrication, and entry swap. See 06-CHANGELOG.md Pass 43.

tasks.title: Supply-chain check on the CVE scanner and license checker themselves
tasks.summary: Verify behavior when OSV.dev is unreachable mid-run, and whether a malicious package could report a clean SBOM to slip past license-checker.ts / cve-scanner.ts.
tasks.whyHard: The security tooling's own failure modes haven't been audited as rigorously as the code it protects -- genuinely easy to overlook.
tasks.notes: Implemented in packages/agent/tests/supply-chain-audit.test.ts. 26 adversarial test cases covering: OSV unreachable/500/malformed, GHSA unreachable, both sources offline, resolved-entry preservation, >1000-component batch limit, CVE alias deduplication, compound SPDX expressions (intentional conservative deny policy documented), GPL suffix variants, missing/empty license, lockfileVersion 2 format, scoped package normalisation, custom override policies, and the self-reported-clean design limit. Two design gaps documented: (1) SPDX compound-expression substring matching is intentionally conservative; (2) lockfile-verbatim trust is a known limit — mitigation via task-42.

tasks.title: Stress-test Darwin Engine's --evolve mode under real regression pressure
tasks.summary: Confirm the 10%-regression revert threshold actually triggers correctly against a real degrading metric stream, including several small compounding regressions.
tasks.whyHard: Needs deliberately adversarial prompt sequences over many cycles.
tasks.notes: Pass 51: darwin-engine-stress.test.ts — 9 describe blocks, 24 adversarial assertions. See packages/agent/docs/51-V24-AUDIT-PASS-51.md

tasks.title: Multi-agent swarm contention testing
tasks.summary: Run genuine concurrent swarm agents against Semantic DAG Lock + per-file locks to surface race conditions that reading code cannot catch.
tasks.whyHard: Needs actual concurrent load, not audit passes -- this is the class of bug that looks fine for 50 passes and then corrupts a real repo on first collision.
tasks.notes: Pass 52: swarm-contention.test.ts — 9 describe blocks, 22 adversarial test cases. Tests the real SemanticDagLock class with an in-process RedisState mock under genuine concurrent load (Promise.all). See packages/agent/docs/52-V24-AUDIT-PASS-52.md

tasks.title: Load-test with a genuinely oversized PR
tasks.summary: Hundreds of changed files, several >500KB, run against the rate limiter and Cartographer -- the scenario most likely to blow the Groq context window or the GitHub API rate limit.
tasks.whyHard: Needs a real oversized repo/PR to simulate; existing k6 scripts exercise the API surface, not this specific shape of load.
tasks.notes: Implemented in packages/agent/tests/cartographer-oversized-pr.test.ts. 8 describe blocks, 25 test cases. Exercises isLargeFile, summarizeFile, buildFileMap with 200-file and 500KB+ synthetic fixtures. Documents GAP-1 (concurrent summarizeFile redundant AI calls) and GAP-2 (Redis stale-hit after content change). See 06-CHANGELOG.md Pass 59 and packages/agent/docs/59-V24-AUDIT-PASS-59.md.

tasks.title: Knip-based dependency audit with real node_modules
tasks.summary: A full unused-dependency audit across all ~100 service files in packages/agent, flagged as open in tasks/dead-code-triage-v24.30.0.md across multiple passes.
tasks.whyHard: Tedious rather than difficult -- needs install access this sandbox doesn't have.
tasks.notes: Requires `npm install` (real node_modules) for knip to resolve the dependency graph. Not startable in a no-network sandbox.

tasks.title: Make the WebRTC Layer 1 test channel real (or formally retire it)
tasks.summary: Add a real Node WebRTC binding (@roamhq/wrtc or werift) so EdgeTestClient can actually originate offers from the CI runner -- currently documented as unreachable by design, not a bug.
tasks.whyHard: Native addon compilation on CI runners; STUN alone likely won't traverse most NATs, so this may also need TURN.
tasks.notes: Possibly low value relative to effort -- Layer 2 already degrades gracefully at near-zero cost. Do not start until task-3's infra keep-or-cut decision confirms this is worth the effort. Also requires network to install the native addon.

tasks.title: Run the actual test suites (npm install && vitest && tsc)
tasks.summary: Precondition for task-1 and for trusting any "fixed" claim from prior changelog passes. Every bug found so far was caught by reading source, not by execution.
tasks.whyHard: Blocked by sandbox network restrictions, not complexity.
tasks.notes: Run this first the moment a networked environment is available -- every other queued item's confidence improves once real vitest/tsc output exists.

tasks.title: Real end-to-end pipeline run
tasks.summary: Run the full architect -> coder -> gate -> commit -> merge loop against a real GitHub repo with real Redis, R2, and LLM credentials -- not a sandbox.
tasks.whyHard: Requires live secrets, real infra spend, and a disposable/test repo to run against safely.
tasks.notes: Blocked by no network/secrets access in the current sandbox. Run after task-2 so a real test/type-check pass has already caught what it can cheaply.

tasks.title: Cross-run learning validation (semantic-cache, Vector Skill Exchange, Hive)
tasks.summary: Confirm these subsystems actually improve output over time (fewer LLM calls, better patch quality) rather than just writing correctly.
tasks.whyHard: Needs many real runs across weeks -- cannot be validated by static reading or a single test run.
tasks.notes: Needs a real, long-running production or staging environment. Not a single-pass task even once network access exists -- track progress across multiple passes.

tasks.title: Real cost model: LLM token spend vs. pipeline run volume
tasks.summary: Connect actual Groq/LLM token spend to run volume at current production scale. Token-optimization work has never been tied to a real dollar figure.
tasks.whyHard: Needs real production traffic data, not sandbox estimates.
tasks.notes: Needs real production billing/usage data. Pair with cost-ledger.ts once that data exists.

tasks.title: Chaos-monkey x circuit-breaker interaction stress test
tasks.summary: chaos-monkey.ts and circuit-breaker.ts are each tested in isolation. Verify circuit-breaker.ts actually opens and later half-closes correctly when chaos-monkey.ts injects failures mid-pipeline across several different phases in the same run, not just against a single isolated call.
tasks.whyHard: Timing-dependent interaction between two independently-correct subsystems -- this repo's audit history shows the highest-risk regressions live at exactly this kind of interaction surface, not inside either subsystem alone.
tasks.notes: See packages/agent/docs/53-V24-AUDIT-PASS-53.md. 9 describe suites, 29 test cases. Confirmed: breaker opens at threshold, no phantom calls while OPEN, HALF_OPEN probe semantics, multi-provider independence, interleaved-success counter reset, concurrent failure safety, and full pipeline lifecycle.

tasks.title: Meta-agent mutation rollback adversarial test
tasks.summary: meta-agent.ts's mutatePrompt/rollbackLastMutation (used from cli.ts) needs an adversarial test proving rollback restores byte-identical prior state after N chained mutations, including a simulated crash/interrupt mid-mutation.
tasks.whyHard: Rollback correctness is easy to prove for one mutation and easy to silently break across a chain of several -- exactly the kind of defect that would only surface after multiple Darwin-engine mutation cycles in production.
tasks.notes: Implemented in packages/agent/tests/meta-agent-rollback.test.ts. 7 describe suites, 32 adversarial test cases. Confirmed: byte-identical restore for chained 7-mutation rollback, crash-after-historyKey-write leaves active unchanged, phantom history entries cleaned idempotently by rollback, 3-crash+1-success scenario fully recoverable, namespace isolation across all three agents. Three design boundaries documented (history cap at 20, non-atomic rollback, phantom entries). See packages/agent/docs/54-V24-AUDIT-PASS-54.md.

tasks.title: Semantic DAG Lock deadlock proof
tasks.summary: Extend task-9's contention testing specifically to deadlock: prove no circular-wait deadlock exists in semantic-dag.ts when multiple concurrent agents request overlapping file-sets in different acquisition orders.
tasks.whyHard: A livelock/deadlock bug can pass hundreds of runs where lock sets happen not to form a cycle, then wedge a real swarm run indefinitely with no exception thrown -- the worst kind of bug to detect via manual review.
tasks.notes: Implemented in packages/agent/tests/semantic-dag-deadlock.test.ts. 20+ test cases across 4 suites: (1) 11 deterministic unit tests covering single-agent, idempotent release, empty set, disjoint files, sequential agents, canonical two-agent/two-resource deadlock scenario, triangular three-agent contention, fully-overlapping hotspot, partial overlap, explicit exclusivity ordering, and post-run clean lock state; (2) 1 contrast test confirming UnsafeLock deadlocks on the canonical scenario (harness validation); (3) 4 property tests (fast-check, 50-500 runs each): forward-progress guarantee, lock-map empty after completion, no concurrent dual-holder, canonical sort invariant; (4) 3 stress tests (20-agent overlap, 10-agent worst-case reverse, 3-wave sequential burst). See packages/agent/docs/48-V24-AUDIT-PASS-48.md.

tasks.title: Obfuscator token-collision exhaustive test at scale
tasks.summary: Pass 27 fixed a specific token-collision bug in obfuscator.ts. Confirm no collision exists across a realistic large symbol corpus (thousands of identifiers, not just the small set that triggered the Pass 27 regression).
tasks.whyHard: The Pass 27 fix proves the specific reported case is fixed; it doesn't prove the collision space is closed at real-world identifier-count scale, where birthday-paradox-style collisions become far more likely than in a small hand-written regression test.
tasks.notes: Exhaustive scale test (1k, 3k, 5k identifiers; multi-file; pre-seeded VAR_N; tokenOffset isolation; reconstituteCode prefix-collision at scale). 9 describe blocks, 33 cases. See packages/agent/docs/55-V24-AUDIT-PASS-55.md and 06-CHANGELOG.md Pass 55.

tasks.title: Trust-ledger / vitals-score gaming resistance
tasks.summary: trust-ledger.ts and vitals-score.ts score agent/patch trustworthiness over time. Check whether an adversarial sequence of patches (many trivial, low-risk patches to inflate a trust score) could let one later large, risky patch slip through review it would otherwise not have earned.
tasks.whyHard: This is a game-theoretic property, not a correctness property -- 'the scorer computes correctly' and 'the scorer can't be gamed by a sequence designed to game it' are different, and only the second is the actual security-relevant guarantee.
tasks.notes: Implemented in packages/agent/tests/trust-ledger-gaming.test.ts. 6 describe suites, 28 test cases. Three gaps found: Gap-1 (auto-merge unlockable in 5 trivial successes from DEFAULT_BOND -- primary structural gap), Gap-2 (confidence underreporting makes failure penalty symmetric with success gain at confidence=0), Gap-3 (classifyTrustCategory complexity override is caller-controlled). Five resistance properties confirmed: cross-category isolation, asymmetric failure recovery, score floor, seed-sealing (probation gate prevents immediate auto-merge), probation stickiness (only cleared at FULL_AUTONOMY_THRESHOLD not PROBATION_THRESHOLD). vitals-score confirmed display-only -- no auto-merge gate attached. See packages/agent/docs/49-V24-AUDIT-PASS-49.md.

tasks.title: Uncertainty-sampling calibration check
tasks.summary: uncertainty-sampling.ts produces confidence outputs. Verify they are actually calibrated -- of all patches scored e.g. '80% confidence,' do roughly 80% actually pass the gate -- rather than merely monotonic/plausible-looking.
tasks.whyHard: Calibration (not just correct ranking) is the property confidence-scorer.ts's own comments say autonomous decisions need, and it's the one that can't be checked by reading the scoring formula -- it requires a labeled outcome distribution.
tasks.notes: Calibration math validated in 8 describe blocks, 42 assertions. Four design boundaries documented (DB-1 through DB-4). See packages/agent/docs/60-V24-AUDIT-PASS-60.md.

tasks.title: Skill-exchange / Hive poisoning test
tasks.summary: vector-skill-exchange.ts and skill-exchange.ts store learned patches for reuse across missions (the Hive). Check whether a bad or subtly-wrong patch stored early can later be retrieved and reapplied to an unrelated mission, propagating a defect instead of a genuine fix.
tasks.whyHard: This is a cross-run data-poisoning concern, not a single-run correctness concern -- the failure mode is invisible in any single mission's test suite and only shows up as a slow quality regression across many future missions that reused the poisoned entry.
tasks.notes: Implemented in packages/agent/tests/hive-poisoning.test.ts. 19 adversarial test cases (4 suites) covering semantic-cache hive, skill-exchange, vector-skill-exchange offline mode, and cross-subsystem consistency. 3 gaps confirmed (GAP-1: near-identical mission retrieval, GAP-2: quarantine eviction via flooding, GAP-3: quarantine bypass via objective mutation) and 3 additional gaps documented (GAP-4: UNTRUSTED_DATA wrapper does not remove content, GAP-5: no content-quality gate on schema-valid skills, GAP-6: name field not wrapped). 9 resistance properties confirmed. See 06-CHANGELOG.md Pass 50.

tasks.title: Model-deprecation-watchdog soft-deprecation detection
tasks.summary: model-deprecation-watchdog.ts currently warns when a configured model is hard-absent from a provider's catalogue. Check whether it also catches 'soft deprecation' -- model still listed but heavily rate-limited, degraded, or being sunset with a published future date -- not just hard absence.
tasks.whyHard: Hard-absence is the easy 90% case; soft deprecation is the harder, more common real-world failure mode and the one most likely to cause silent quality/latency degradation before anyone notices a model is on its way out.
tasks.notes: Soft-deprecation audit: 7 describe blocks, 24 assertions. Six gaps documented (GAP-1 through GAP-7, note GAP-6 is High). See packages/agent/docs/61-V24-AUDIT-PASS-61.md.

tasks.title: Quota-guardian / cost-ledger concurrent reconciliation
tasks.summary: quota-guardian.ts and cost-ledger.ts both gate spend. Confirm they agree under concurrent runs -- e.g. two runs simultaneously approaching a shared quota -- rather than each independently under-counting the other's in-flight spend and jointly overshooting.
tasks.whyHard: Each system is presumably correct against its own sequential view of spend; the bug (if any) only appears when two concurrent views should have been reconciled against a single shared ledger and weren't.
tasks.notes: Pass 56: quota-ledger-concurrency.test.ts (8 suites, 28 cases). GAP-1 (High): recordCost non-atomic RMW. GAP-2 (Medium): concurrent headroom reads. See 06-CHANGELOG.md Pass 56 entry.

tasks.title: Hot-reload-config race condition test
tasks.summary: hot-reload-config.ts reloads configuration live. Check for a race where an in-flight phase reads a partially-updated config mid-reload (e.g. new allowedPaths already applied but old blockedPaths still in effect), producing an inconsistent path-guard state for that phase.
tasks.whyHard: A config reload that isn't atomic from a reader's point of view is a classic TOCTOU-shaped bug that unit tests against the reload function alone won't catch -- it only shows up when a reader is deliberately made to observe the reload mid-flight.
tasks.notes: Implemented in packages/agent/tests/hot-reload-race.test.ts. GAP-1 (Medium): async reader TOCTOU — loadPathGuardConfig is immune today (synchronous). GAP-2 (Low-Medium): consecutive partial-reload window is real for any reader. Safe pattern documented. See 06-CHANGELOG.md Pass 57.

tasks.title: DOM-xray / shadow-traffic validator starvation audit
tasks.summary: dom-xray.ts and shadow-traffic.ts validate UI/traffic behavior. Check whether an adversarial patch could pass both by only behaving correctly during the validators' specific, narrow observation window (e.g. a component that renders correctly on first paint but degrades shortly after).
tasks.whyHard: This is the UI-validator analogue of task-8/task-11's adversarial framing -- 'renders correctly when the validator is watching' and 'renders correctly' are different guarantees, and only an adversarial attempt (not a happy-path test) distinguishes them.
tasks.notes: Starvation audit: 8 describe blocks, 26 assertions. Documents GAP-1 through GAP-8 and four design boundaries (DB-1 through DB-4). High-severity finding: bypass-header attack (DB-3) defeats both validators simultaneously. See packages/agent/docs/62-V24-AUDIT-PASS-62.md.

tasks.title: Compliance-oracle / SBOM / license-checker cross-consistency check
tasks.summary: compliance-oracle.ts opens PRs based on a compliance scan; sbom-generator.ts and license-checker.ts independently report the current dependency tree. Verify the oracle's PRs are actually consistent with what the SBOM/license checker currently report, rather than each subsystem holding a slightly stale independent view.
tasks.whyHard: Three subsystems that each read the dependency tree independently can silently drift out of sync with each other over time even if each is individually correct against the tree at the moment it last read it.
tasks.notes: Implemented in packages/agent/tests/compliance-cross-consistency.test.ts. 8 describe blocks, 31 test cases. Confirms: enumeration count/name/version consistency between SBOM and license-checker; license string agreement for non-empty licenses; documents GAP-1 (Medium — missing license normalization divergence: sbom-generator returns "" → omits licenses field, license-checker returns "UNKNOWN" → flags unknown violation, creating inconsistent operator signals for the same package); GAP-2 (Low — empty string license: same divergence pattern); and four design boundaries (DB-1 object-style license consistent, DB-2 orthogonal scopes, DB-3 root-package skip consistent, DB-4 name normalization identical). See packages/agent/docs/63-V24-AUDIT-PASS-63.md.

tasks.title: API-contract-guard adversarial schema-drift test
tasks.summary: api-contract-guard.ts is meant to catch schema drift in architect-schema.ts / coder-schema.ts / reviewer-schema.ts. Adversarially test whether a patch can add or change a field in a way that's actually load-bearing at runtime but reads as a harmless optional-field addition to the guard.
tasks.whyHard: Schema guards are usually validated against obviously-breaking changes (removing a required field); the harder, more realistic failure mode is a change that looks additive/safe to a naive schema diff but changes real runtime behavior.
tasks.notes: Implemented in packages/agent/tests/api-contract-guard-adversarial.test.ts. 7 describe blocks, 21 test cases. Documents 7 gaps: GAP-1 through GAP-5 (OpenAPI), GAP-6 and GAP-7 (GraphQL). See 06-CHANGELOG.md Pass 58 and packages/agent/docs/58-V24-AUDIT-PASS-58.md for full impact analysis.

tasks.title: Retry / circuit-breaker double-execution safety audit
tasks.summary: retry.ts combined with circuit-breaker.ts wraps operations with side effects (e.g. GitHub API writes via github-client.ts). Confirm a retried operation can't execute twice if a timeout races a successful-but-slow response, absent an idempotency key.
tasks.whyHard: This is a real, well-known distributed-systems bug class (retry-induced double-execution of a non-idempotent write) that's invisible in a happy-path retry test and only appears when a response is slow enough to trigger a retry that races the original request's actual completion.
tasks.notes: Adversarial test suite added: packages/agent/tests/retry-double-execution.test.ts — 8 describe blocks, 24 assertions covering no-double-execution on success, non-retryable status classification (409/422/405/403/404/400/401 all blocked), maxAttempts:1 single-shot guarantee, isHttpRetryable classification, onRetry hook timing, and exhaustion boundary. See CHANGELOG.md Pass 40 entry.

tasks.title: Prompt-registry version-rollback mid-run consistency check
tasks.summary: prompt-registry.ts versions prompts. Confirm that rolling back to a previous prompt version mid-run doesn't leave one phase (e.g. architect) on the new prompt semantics while another phase (e.g. reviewer) in the same run is still on the old version, producing an internally inconsistent interpretation of the same objective within a single mission.
tasks.whyHard: A per-phase-lazy prompt lookup (rather than one resolved-and-cached-at-run-start version) is an easy thing to get subtly wrong, and the resulting bug is a mission that behaves inconsistently with itself rather than throwing any error.
tasks.notes: Implemented in packages/agent/tests/prompt-registry-mid-run-consistency.test.ts. 8 describe blocks, 32 test cases. Confirms design contract: getActivePrompt() is a live readFileSync on every call — no in-process cache, no per-run isolation. Documents GAP-1 (Medium — manual rollback mid-run causes silent phase divergence: phase 1 sees vN, rollback fires, phase 2 sees v(N-1), no error raised); GAP-2 (Medium — auto-rollback mid-run: 5 results with successRate < 0.70 triggers auto-rollback synchronously within recordPromptResult, so a phase own poor results can switch the prompt version seen by subsequent phases). Documents safe caller pattern: snapshot all prompts at run-start. Confirms DB-1 (live read), DB-2 (caller-snapshot mitigation), DB-3 (auto-rollback threshold runs>=5 AND <0.70), DB-4 (multi-key independence), DB-5 (single-step rollback), DB-6 (stats saved before auto-rollback). See packages/agent/docs/64-V24-AUDIT-PASS-64.md.

tasks.title: Decide on additional OpenAI-compatible LLM race candidates (Fireworks, DeepInfra, Novita, CF Workers AI REST)
tasks.summary: Round 3 free-tier survey found more OpenAI-compatible endpoints not yet in the ai-router.ts race: Fireworks AI (small free trial credit), DeepInfra (very cheap/occasionally free credits), Novita AI (free trial credits), and Cloudflare Workers AI's plain REST API (separate free daily allotment from the existing env.AI binding used in Tier 1). Decide which, if any, are worth adding to the race.
tasks.whyHard: Organizational, not technical -- similar in kind to task-3's keep-or-cut decision, but scoped to LLM race candidates specifically rather than Tier 2/3 infra. Each addition also means a new account/key to manage.
tasks.notes: Decision: YES on all four. Fireworks (accounts/fireworks/models/llama-v3p1-8b-instruct), DeepInfra (meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct), Novita (meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b-instruct), CF Workers AI REST (@cf/meta/llama-3.1-8b-instruct, separate daily allotment from Tier-1 V8 binding). New env keys: FIREWORKS_API_KEY, DEEPINFRA_API_KEY, NOVITA_API_KEY, CF_ACCOUNT_ID, CF_AI_API_TOKEN. Tests: provider-race-a3.test.ts (8 describe blocks, 28 cases). See packages/agent/docs/71-V24-AUDIT-PASS-71.md.

tasks.title: Decide whether to prep multimodal (speech/vision) free tiers ahead of an actual consumer
tasks.summary: Groq already serves free-tier Whisper (speech-to-text) and some vision models under the same API key already in use; Google AI Studio's free Gemini tier includes vision input under the same GEMINI_API_KEY already wired. Neither ui-synthesizer.ts nor dom-xray.ts currently consumes image/audio input. Decide whether to stub this in now (cheap, same keys) or explicitly defer until a real consumer exists.
tasks.whyHard: Not a hard engineering call, but a scope-creep judgment call -- wiring unused capability ahead of a consumer is exactly the kind of thing that inflates surface area without value if the consumer never materializes.
tasks.notes: Source: free-tier-energy-ideas-round3.md, section 2. Lowest priority of this batch precisely because there is no current consumer -- do not build speculative plumbing without an explicit decision to do so.

tasks.title: Decide on free CI/build-acceleration caching (Turborepo remote cache via Vercel, or Nx Cloud)
tasks.summary: This is already a workspace-style monorepo (packages/agent, apps/mission-control). A shared build cache (Turborepo remote caching, free via Vercel) could cut npm run build time in CI at no cost; Nx Cloud is the equivalent if the project ever migrates to Nx. Decide whether to adopt either.
tasks.whyHard: Organizational -- needs a decision on adopting Turborepo (a build-orchestration change, not just a cache flag) before any code changes, similar in kind to task-3.
tasks.notes: Decision: Turborepo remote cache CONDITIONAL-YES (3 preconditions: C1 build/tsc ≥20% CI runtime; C2 TURBO_TOKEN+TURBO_TEAM available as scoped Vercel secrets; C3 secrets in GitHub Actions before workflow mutation). Nx Cloud NO-GO — requires full Nx migration not planned. Config spec and adoption path documented in packages/agent/docs/72-V24-AUDIT-PASS-72.md PASS 5 and 03-ARCHITECTURE.md §CI Caching Decision.

tasks.title: Decide on centralized secrets/config management (Doppler or Infisical) vs. current bootstrap.mjs approach
tasks.summary: Doppler's free tier centralizes env vars across dev/CI/prod with a UI instead of hand-editing .env and GitHub Secrets separately; Infisical is the open-source equivalent. Both could reduce the exact friction bootstrap.mjs exists to solve. Decide whether either is worth adopting over the status quo.
tasks.whyHard: Organizational -- introducing a third-party secrets manager (even free-tier) is a security-relevant infra decision, not a pure engineering task.
tasks.notes: Decision: STATUS QUO KEPT. Doppler NO-GO (3 blockers: SaaS trust boundary over PRIVACY_MODE=strict path; 1-user free tier; bootstrap.mjs already solves stated friction). Infisical cloud NO-GO (same SaaS trust blocker). Infisical self-hosted NO-GO (requires always-on dedicated service not in any infra tier, contradicts minimal-infra posture). Two bootstrap.mjs improvements identified for future code pass: --verify flag and grouped summary output. See packages/agent/docs/73-V24-AUDIT-PASS-73.md and 03-ARCHITECTURE.md §Secrets Management Decision.

tasks.title: Decide on Cloudflare AI Gateway as a caching/rate-limit proxy in front of the ai-router race
tasks.summary: Cloudflare's free AI Gateway sits in front of any of the existing LLM race candidates, caches identical requests, and gives free per-provider analytics -- a softer lever than adding another provider account, and it reuses the Cloudflare account already in play for Workers AI.
tasks.whyHard: Lower friction than task-31/task-34 since the CF account already exists, but still changes the request path for every provider in the race and needs an explicit go/no-go before touching ai-router.ts.
tasks.notes: Decision: NO-GO. Four independent blockers (each individually sufficient): B1 — Tier-1 CF Workers AI uses V8 runtime binding, not HTTP, so gateway cannot proxy the most cost-sensitive free-tier path; B2 — routing through CF request logging increases trust surface for PRIVACY_MODE=strict runs; B3 — ~0% cache hit rate given run-specific + commit-specific prompt content; B4 — quota-guardian already tracks per-provider headroom programmatically, adding gateway creates unreconciled duplicate state. All four conditions must be resolved before revisiting. See packages/agent/docs/65-V24-AUDIT-PASS-65.md PASS 5 for full conditions.

tasks.title: Decide on second-source code-quality/security APIs (Snyk, Socket.dev, VirusTotal)
tasks.summary: Snyk's free-tier API could feed cve-scanner.ts as a second, independent source alongside OSV.dev; Socket.dev's free API flags npm supply-chain risk (typosquatting, install scripts, obfuscated code) for sbom-generator.ts/license-checker.ts; VirusTotal's free public API could let dry-run.ts/the sandbox check a downloaded dependency's hash against known-bad reputation data. Decide which, if any, are worth the new account overhead.
tasks.whyHard: Each is a new third-party account feeding a security-relevant gate -- worth a deliberate decision on redundancy value vs. added attack surface/maintenance, not just 'more signal is always better'.
tasks.notes: Source: free-tier-energy-ideas-round4-apis.md, section 1. Pairs with task-13's supply-chain audit of the existing CVE scanner/license checker -- resolve task-13's findings first if they reveal gaps these new sources would actually close. Completed Pass 67. Owner decision: implement all three. New files: integrations/socket-risk.ts, integrations/virustotal.ts. Modified: cve-scanner.ts (Snyk D4 + sourceCounts), sbom-generator.ts (enrichSbomWithSocketRisk), license-checker.ts (checkSocketSupplyChain), dry-run.ts (setVirusTotalFindings), env-validator.ts (3 new optional keys). Tests: security-api-sources.test.ts (9 describe blocks, 28 cases). See packages/agent/docs/67-V24-AUDIT-PASS-67.md.

tasks.title: Decide on code-intelligence enrichment APIs (Sourcegraph public search, GitHub code-search/dependency-graph endpoints)
tasks.summary: Sourcegraph's public API (free for public code search) could let context-enricher.ts pull real-world usage examples of an API the Coder agent is about to call. Separately, GitHub's own REST/GraphQL code-search and dependency-graph endpoints are free with the GITHUB_TOKEN already in use, and cartographer.ts/dependency-graph.ts could call them directly instead of reconstructing that info via LLM calls -- this half needs no new account.
tasks.whyHard: Two different friction levels bundled in one idea: the GitHub-endpoint half is a low-risk implementation task with no new decision needed, while the Sourcegraph half is a new third-party dependency needing an explicit adopt/skip call -- split them if the GitHub half is picked up first.
tasks.notes: GitHub-endpoint half implemented in Pass 69. New file: integrations/github-dependency-graph.ts (fetchGitHubSbom, crossCheckDependencyGraph, annotateGraphWithGitHubSbom). Tests: github-dependency-graph.test.ts (9 describe blocks, 27 cases). Sourcegraph half deferred — still requiresOwnerDecision for that scoped piece. See packages/agent/docs/69-V24-AUDIT-PASS-69.md.

tasks.title: Decide on visual-regression/cross-browser QA APIs (BrowserStack, Percy)
tasks.summary: BrowserStack's free tier (limited minutes) offers real cross-browser testing relevant if dom-xray.ts/shadow-traffic.ts ever need to validate a UI change beyond a single headless browser; Percy's free tier does screenshot-diffing, a natural pairing with dom-xray.ts's existing DOM-diff gate. Both are rate-limited enough to be 'occasional use' rather than every-run.
tasks.whyHard: Organizational -- adopting either means budgeting scarce free minutes/snapshots across runs, a policy decision as much as a technical one.
tasks.notes: BrowserStack: NO-GO. Three independent blockers: B1 free-tier exhaustion (100 min/month), B2 no rendering phase in pipeline, B3 no cross-browser requirement documented. Percy: NO-GO now; CONDITIONAL-YES when pipeline gains a render-and-snapshot phase or dom-xray.ts produces rendered HTML output. Percy preferred over BrowserStack Visual when conditions met (5000 snapshots/month free, no session overhead). See packages/agent/docs/70-V24-AUDIT-PASS-70.md PASS 5.

tasks.title: Decide on feature-flag-gated canary rollout (LaunchDarkly or Flagsmith)
tasks.summary: LaunchDarkly's free tier is a real feature-flag API that could let canary.ts gate a change behind a flag instead of only edge-traffic percentage -- useful for changes that aren't purely edge/network-routable. Flagsmith is the open-source equivalent if avoiding another SaaS dependency matters. The source survey flagged this as one of the two ideas 'worth implementing soon' out of its whole round.
tasks.whyHard: Organizational -- picking a feature-flag vendor (or the OSS route) is a real architectural commitment for canary.ts, not a drop-in addition, and needs a documented choice before implementation.
tasks.notes: Source: free-tier-energy-ideas-round5.md, section 1. Prioritized above the rest of the Round 5 batch because the source doc itself singled this out as worth pursuing soon rather than merely situational. Completed Pass 68. Owner decision: LaunchDarkly over Flagsmith. New file: integrations/launchdarkly.ts (evaluateFlag, isCanaryEnabled). Modified: canary.ts (routeTrafficWithFeatureFlag, CanaryRoutingResult), env-validator.ts (LD_SDK_KEY). Tests: launchdarkly-canary.test.ts (9 describe blocks, 22 cases). See packages/agent/docs/68-V24-AUDIT-PASS-68.md.

tasks.title: Decide whether to prep i18n (LibreTranslate) ahead of any multi-language UI-copy requirement
tasks.summary: LibreTranslate's free public instance (or self-host) is open-source and keyless, and would only matter if ui-synthesizer.ts ever generates user-facing copy needing more than one language -- which it does not today.
tasks.whyHard: Purely a product-roadmap question (is multi-language UI copy generation ever planned?), not an engineering one -- the source survey itself flags this as speculative.
tasks.notes: Source: free-tier-energy-ideas-round5.md, section 3. Lowest priority in this batch; do not build i18n plumbing without an explicit yes to the underlying product question first.

tasks.title: Cross-check dependency metadata against keyless deps.dev and free-tier Libraries.io
tasks.summary: deps.dev (Google, free, no key) offers dependency metadata/graph info dependency-graph.ts could cross-check against; Libraries.io's free tier adds package popularity/maintenance signal that confidence-scorer.ts could use to lower confidence when a patch adds a barely-maintained dependency.
tasks.whyHard: Not conceptually hard, but genuinely needs live network access to the real endpoints to validate the integration -- this is an implementation task, not a decision, since deps.dev needs no signup and Libraries.io's free key is low-friction.
tasks.notes: Source: free-tier-energy-ideas-round4-apis.md, section 4. Blocked purely by the current sandbox's lack of network access, not by any organizational decision -- eligible to start the moment a networked environment is available.

tasks.title: Add ClearlyDefined and SPDX as a second license-data source in license-checker.ts
tasks.summary: ClearlyDefined's API (free, no key) provides crowd-sourced license data for packages where package.json license fields are missing or wrong; the SPDX license list API (free, no key) gives canonical identifiers for normalizing whatever string a package.json puts in `license`. The source survey flagged this, alongside feature flags (task-39), as one of the two ideas 'worth implementing soon'.
tasks.whyHard: Both sources are keyless and low-friction, so the real work is the integration and reconciliation logic in license-checker.ts (what happens when ClearlyDefined and the lockfile disagree), which needs live calls to validate.
tasks.notes: Source: free-tier-energy-ideas-round5.md, section 2. Prioritized above most other network-blocked items in this batch because the source doc singled it out; pick this up first once network access exists.

tasks.title: Add Discord webhook and ntfy.sh as alerting-rules.ts notification targets
tasks.summary: Discord webhooks need only a webhook URL (same integration shape as the existing SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL) for teams that live in Discord instead of Slack; ntfy.sh is free, open-source push notification with no account required for basic use -- the simplest possible 'ping my phone when a gate fails' option.
tasks.whyHard: Genuinely low-friction, which is exactly why it's low priority here -- mirrors an existing, already-solved integration shape (Slack) rather than introducing new architecture.
tasks.notes: Source: free-tier-energy-ideas-round4-apis.md, section 5. Blocked only by sandbox network access; trivial to validate once available since it's the same pattern as the existing Slack webhook.

tasks.title: Add Wikipedia/Wikidata and archive.org as keyless ground-truth/dead-link checks
tasks.summary: The Wikipedia/Wikidata API (free, no key) could give rationale-bank.ts (or any agent) a factual grounding check unrelated to code, e.g. verifying a claim in a generated doc/comment; archive.org's legitimate API (free) could let api-contract-guard.ts verify external documentation links a patch references haven't rotted.
tasks.whyHard: The source survey itself calls this 'a stretch' -- not obviously useful today, included for completeness rather than an identified real gap.
tasks.notes: Source: free-tier-energy-ideas-round4-apis.md, section 6. Lowest-conviction item in the Round 4 survey; revisit only if a concrete need for factual grounding or dead-link checking actually surfaces.

tasks.title: Operational utility APIs: provider-status preflight check, business-hours timing, and a keyless onboarding demo target
tasks.summary: statuspage.io's free JSON endpoints (published by Vercel, Upstash, Cloudflare, GitHub, among providers already in this stack) could let preflight-estimator.ts check configured providers' status before a run starts and warn instead of silently timing out mid-run; WorldTimeAPI (free, no key) removes any need to hardcode timezone logic in phase-runner.ts if a run ever needs to reason about a target repo team's business hours; JSONPlaceholder-style free public test APIs give dry-run.ts (or a new user's first try) a toy backend to demo against without needing a real one.
tasks.whyHard: Three small, unrelated conveniences bundled together because each is individually minor -- genuinely useful but none blocks anything today, hence the lowest priority tier.
tasks.notes: Source: free-tier-energy-ideas-round5.md, sections 4-6. Consider splitting into separate tasks if one of the three (most likely the preflight status-page check) turns out to matter more than the other two once picked up.

tasks.title: Warden multi-violation reporting and priority-ordering correctness audit
tasks.summary: warden.ts inspectFile() runs three sequential loops with early-return on first match (any > console.log > unwrapped-await). A file with multiple violation types receives exactly one rejection per wardenGuard() call; warden-memory.ts records only the first violation; loadWardenLessons() feeds only that lesson back into the Coder prompt. The priority ordering (any > console.log > await) is undocumented — it is an artifact of loop sequencing, not a stated policy. Existing warden.test.ts covers only single-violation cases.
tasks.whyHard: Not architecturally hard — the inspectFile() logic is simple. The difficulty is deciding whether the fix is: (a) collect-all-violations before returning (more feedback, slightly more ts-morph work), or (b) document the current priority ordering as intentional policy and add tests that lock it in. Either approach is valid and locally executable.
tasks.notes: Completed Pass 66. 8 describe blocks, 32 test cases in warden-multi-violation.test.ts. Documents GAP-1 (undocumented priority ordering any > console.log > await), GAP-2 (N round-trips for N violations), GAP-3 (wardenGuard stops at first violating file), GAP-4 (warden-memory records only first violation per guard call). Gaps documented not fixed — owner decision needed on Option A (collect-all) vs Option B (document-priority). See packages/agent/docs/66-V24-AUDIT-PASS-66.md PASS 5.

tasks.title: Replace USD-only cost tracking with per-provider quota-gauge tracking
tasks.summary: cost-ledger.ts / preflight-estimator.ts currently model spend as a single USD number. For an all-free-tier deployment (Groq, Gemini AI Studio, Neon, Upstash, Axiom, Cloudflare) the scarce resource per provider is its own daily/monthly quota window, not dollars. Add an EnergyQuotaState structure (one QuotaGauge per provider: used, limit, resetsAt, percentUsed) alongside the existing USD figures, and have cost-anomaly-detector-style logic alert on 'about to exhaust quota before reset' rather than only 'spent too much money'.
tasks.whyHard: Requires touching the shared cost-tracking data model without breaking the existing USD-based reporting that owners already read; needs a design for multiple independent reset clocks (per-minute, per-day, per-month) coexisting cleanly.
tasks.notes: Investigation found an existing, mature, header-driven live quota tracker already at services/quota-guardian.ts (not cost-ledger.ts/preflight-estimator.ts, which task-47 assumed) -- extended it rather than building a second, separately-maintained EnergyQuotaState with hardcoded limits that would drift out of date. Added optional requestsLimit/tokensLimit to QuotaSnapshot, quotaPercentUsed()/isNearExhaustion()/getQuotaHealthReport() (the literal "alert before exhaustion" ask), and wired a quotaWarning into preflight-estimator.ts summaryLine/recommendation so it surfaces "alongside the existing USD figures". Also fixed a real pre-existing bug found while implementing: the openrouter HEADER_MAP entry read the LIMIT header into the REMAINING slot (the only provider in the table that did), which would have made OpenRouter always look like it had full headroom. New test file quota-health.test.ts; every quotaPercentUsed/isNearExhaustion/getQuotaHealthReport assertion (19 cases including the 90% boundary and the openrouter-fix scenario) was executed for real with plain node against the exact algorithm -- see docs/history/audits/76-V24-AUDIT-PASS-76.md. No sacred files touched. Differential typecheck (same method as Pass 75) shows zero new error categories from quota-guardian.ts or preflight-estimator.ts specifically. npm test -w @qodo/agent still owed before merge (no network/node_modules in the authoring sandbox).

tasks.title: Free-tier backing-store decision: Neon / Upstash / Cloudflare D1 vs current Tier 2/3 stack
tasks.summary: task-3 (Pass 42) already made a keep-or-cut call on Redis/R2/Vercel/Worker/QStash. Revisit specifically for a $0-budget deployment target: is the durable-state layer (cost-ledger, audit-log, run-state) better served by Neon's per-project free branching Postgres, Upstash's free Redis, or Cloudflare D1 -- given the project is already on Cloudflare Workers for the telemetry proxy?
tasks.whyHard: Organizational, not technical -- a real owner call on which free-tier vendor to standardize on, with real migration cost if reversed later.
tasks.notes: Derived from the 2026-07-08 energy-taxonomy note's 'durable state' and 'ephemeral cache' categories. This is a decision-only pass per the task-3/task-32/task-40 pattern -- do not write migration code speculatively; document the decision and the trigger condition for reversing it.

tasks.title: Evaluate GitHub Actions/Issues as a free queue + task-board backend for this repo's own task queue
tasks.summary: tasks/agent-task-queue.json is hand-maintained JSON. Evaluate whether GitHub Issues (via the API, already reachable through the github-issues.ts integration) plus a `schedule:`-triggered GitHub Actions workflow could replace or front the JSON file, giving a free web UI (Issues board) for humans without adding a paid service.
tasks.whyHard: Organizational/architectural decision with real migration cost (every existing task ID and blockedBy reference would need a mapping); not obviously worth it just because it is free.
tasks.notes: Derived from the 2026-07-08 energy-taxonomy note's 'use GitHub itself as free storage/compute/queue' suggestion. If the decision is NO, record why (e.g. 'JSON + task-queue.mjs is simpler and already works') rather than leaving this silently unresolved.

tasks.title: Evaluate TPU Research Cloud and an idle-device Tailscale mesh as free heavy-compute backends
tasks.summary: darwin-engine.ts and meta-agent mutation testing are the two subsystems most likely to need genuinely heavy batch compute (large-scale simulation, many parallel mutation trials). Evaluate (a) applying to Google's TPU Research Cloud program for burst batch work, and (b) meshing the operator's own idle personal devices via Tailscale + Ollama as a zero-marginal-cost overflow pool, against just staying on the current single-host model.
tasks.whyHard: Requires an actual external application (TRC) with an uncertain approval timeline, and/or hardware the owner may or may not have available -- not resolvable by writing more code alone.
tasks.notes: Derived from the 2026-07-08 energy-taxonomy note. TRC explicitly accepts independent tinkerers/entrepreneurs, not only academics, but does require sharing the resulting work publicly -- confirm the owner is comfortable with that condition before applying.

tasks.title: Surface per-provider quota gauges in the mission-control dashboard
tasks.summary: Once task-47's EnergyQuotaState exists, add a dashboard panel (apps/mission-control) showing each free-tier provider's current usage against its reset window, so an operator can see 'Groq: 62% of daily quota, resets in 4h' at a glance instead of discovering a 429 mid-run.
tasks.whyHard: Needs a new TelemetryContext data path end-to-end (Worker -> dashboard) without duplicating the existing cost/SLO panels, and has to stay useful even when some providers are unconfigured.
tasks.notes: Pure implementation task once task-47 lands. Before building a new panel from scratch, check whether the existing SLO/cost widgets can be generalized instead of adding a fourth parallel dashboard component, per tasks/AGENT-PRINCIPLES.md.

tasks.title: Admin Decisions panel: surface every owner-decision-gated task in the dashboard with a one-click resolve
tasks.summary: Tasks with requiresOwnerDecision: true (e.g. task-32, task-40, task-48, task-49, task-50) currently require someone to hand-edit tasks/agent-task-queue.json to resolve. Add a small, clearly-labeled panel to apps/mission-control that lists every such task still in 'queued' status, shows its summary/whyHard, and lets an admin record a decision (and optionally free-text rationale) that writes back to the queue file (or an equivalent store) -- so the admin never has to touch raw JSON to unblock the pipeline.
tasks.whyHard: Needs a real write path from the dashboard back into repo state (or a small backing store), which is more than a read-only telemetry panel -- has to be designed so an agent can't be tricked into treating a UI click as a substitute for an actual, reasoned owner decision.
tasks.notes: Requested directly by the project owner (2026-07-08): owner-decision-gated tasks should be easy to resolve from an admin board rather than by hand-editing JSON. Write path must require an explicit decision + rationale per task, not a bare status flip, so 'done' still means a real decision was recorded, not just dismissed.

tasks.title: Add a readyToArchive marker + archive command so verified-done tasks can be pruned from the visible queue
tasks.summary: Completed tasks currently stay in tasks/agent-task-queue.json forever, growing the file indefinitely. Add a `readyToArchive: boolean` field (set automatically once a task is status:'done' AND its corresponding validate.sh / test run has been confirmed green in that same pass), a `node scripts/task-queue.mjs archive <id>` command that moves the task's full record into a new tasks/agent-task-queue-archive.json (never deletes history, only relocates it), and a corresponding one-click 'Archive verified-done tasks' action in the admin panel from task-52.
tasks.whyHard: Needs to guarantee no task is archived (and its history effectively hidden from the active view) unless it was both completed AND actually re-verified working -- an agent marking its own work 'ready to archive' without genuine re-verification would quietly erode the audit trail this whole queue exists to provide.
tasks.notes: Requested directly by the project owner (2026-07-08): tasks that are done and already tested should be clearly marked for cleanup, but never silently deleted -- archive to a separate file, don't erase. Reuse audit-log.ts's append-only pattern for the archive file if practical, rather than inventing a new storage format.

tasks.title: Revisit the CIEP 'one task per pass' throughput limit for a more scalable, self-improving queue protocol
tasks.summary: The current protocol (see 06-CHANGELOG.md and this file's own top-level description) processes exactly one queued task per pass, in strict priority order. Requested directly by the project owner (2026-07-08): this ceiling should be revisited so the queue can be run more professionally at scale -- e.g. allowing multiple independent (non-blockedBy-related) tasks to be processed within a single pass when they touch disjoint files/subsystems, and having the protocol itself track its own throughput/cycle-time over passes and propose adjustments to its own rules when the data supports it.
tasks.whyHard: This is a protocol/meta-process change, not a code change -- it affects every future pass's discipline and audit trail, and a badly-designed relaxation could let unrelated changes get bundled together in ways that make rollback and review harder, defeating the reason the one-task-per-pass rule exists in the first place.
tasks.notes: Do not just remove the limit outright. Propose a concrete replacement rule (e.g. 'up to N tasks per pass IF their touched-file-sets are provably disjoint AND each still gets its own Impact Analysis + changelog subsection') and get it recorded as an explicit owner decision here before any future pass relies on it. This task is itself an instance of what it asks for: think about a better mechanism before just lifting the cap.

tasks.title: Receipt lineage across relay hops (composability primitive)
tasks.summary: Optional lineage block on qodo.receipt/v1 (hopIndex, parentReceiptSha256, genesis) plus an optional genesis parameter on appendAuditEntry/verifyAuditChain, so a relay hop can seed its audit chain with the sha256 of the actual prior hop receipt instead of the fixed all-zero genesis. Verifier recomputes the parent hash itself rather than trusting the child receipt claim.
tasks.whyHard: Cross-hop composability without a shared trust anchor between stateless agent instances -- the existing receipt/audit-chain primitive only proved a single run happened under controls, not that one run followed another. Required extending two files (one sacred) additively without breaking any existing receipt or call site.
tasks.notes: Implemented in audit-log.ts (sacred, additive optional genesis param), receipt.ts (lineage field + verifyReceipt opts.parentReceipt), scripts/verify-receipt.mjs (--parent-receipt flag, mirrors receipt.ts). Standalone script logic was executed for real against a hand-built two-hop fixture pair (see docs/history/audits/74-V24-AUDIT-PASS-74.md); the TS-level vitest suite (receipt-lineage.test.ts) and typecheck could NOT be run in the authoring sandbox (no network, no node_modules) -- run npm test -w @qodo/agent and npm run typecheck before merging. Sacred manifest rebaselined for audit-log.ts.

tasks.title: Wire cli.ts to read an incoming parent-receipt at pipeline start
tasks.summary: Automate what task-55 makes possible: at pipeline bootstrap, check for a relay-handoff parent-receipt file, compute its sha256, thread it through as this run genesis (audit-log.ts) and populate receipt.lineage (receipt-emitter.ts) without any manual step.
tasks.whyHard: Touches cli.ts, the second sacred file in this area (phase state machine) -- needs an explicit, reviewed decision on the on-disk convention for a relay handoff artifact (fixed filename? env var? CLI flag?) before landing, per AGENT-PRINCIPLES.md #1/#2. Deliberately NOT bundled into task-55 to keep that pass reviewable and its blast radius honest.
tasks.notes: Implemented in packages/agent/src/pipeline/relay-lineage.ts (new, non-sacred): resolveRelayLineage() reads .relay-parent-receipt.json if present, computes sha256(canonicalJson(parent)) via node:crypto directly, caches per-process. Wired into helpers.ts audit() (every appendAuditEntry call now threads the resolved genesis) and receipt-emitter.ts emitReceipt() (populates receipt.lineage automatically when a parent was found). Correction to task-55 scope note: cli.ts run-pipeline bootstrap is NOT where the audit chain/receipt actually start (thats run-pipeline.ts, not sacred) -- but cli.ts DID need one small additive fix: the --rehearse pre-flight appends rehearsal-completed/-blocked BEFORE run-pipeline.ts runs, so it can be the true first chain entry and needed the same genesis threaded in. Sacred manifest rebaselined for cli.ts. Differential typecheck (global tsc, no node_modules available) against an unmodified baseline copy showed ZERO new error categories introduced, only the pre-existing @types/node-missing noise already present throughout this sandbox -- see docs/history/audits/75-V24-AUDIT-PASS-75.md for the full transcript. vitest itself still could not run (no network/node_modules); run npm test -w @qodo/agent before merging.
